title: Lorlatinib Plus TNG462 in ALK+ MTAP Del NSCLC
official: TAP-ALK: A Phase I/II Study of TNG462 in Combination With Lorlatinib in MTAP-Deleted, ALK-Rearranged NSCLC Following Progression on Prior TKI Therapy
summary: TAP-ALK is a DF/HCC investigator-sponsored interventional study of TNG462 (vopimetostat) in combination with lorlatinib for participants with MTAP-deleted, ALK-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) following progression on prior tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. The study is being conducted under IND 183798 and plans to enroll 30 participants.
conditions: ALK Positive Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 18 years
* Histologically or cytologically confirmed NSCLC harboring an ALK rearrangement, documented by an FDA/EMA-approved or validated local test.
* Confirmed MTAP loss, demonstrated by immunohistochemistry (IHC) as complete loss in the presence of a positive internal control, or homozygous deletion by next-generation sequencing (NGS) in a CLIA-/ISO-accredited laboratory. The Sponsor-Investigator will review molecular testing to confirm eligibility (central reading of the IHC sample and/or repeat MTAP staining on archival tissue; check of the NGS report). Cases with heterogenous MTAP loss in IHC defined as MTAP loss in at least 80% of the tumor cells but less than 100%, may be included with the permission of the Sponsor-Investigator and after central revision of the slides.
* Radiographic disease progression after at least one or more ALK TKIs, including prior lorlatinib therapy. Prior chemotherapy and prior neladalkib (NVL-655) are allowed
* At least one measurable extracranial lesion according to RECIST v1.1.
* ECOG performance status 0-1 (Appendix A). ECOG performance status 2 may be allowed with the permission of the Sponsor-Investigator
* Adequate organ and marrow function, defined as:

  * ANC ≥ 1.5 × 10⁹/L
  * Platelets ≥ 75 × 10⁹/L, without platelet transfusion within 7 days prior to screening hematology assessment
  * Hemoglobin \> 8.5 g/dL without transfusion within 14 days prior to screening hematology assessment
  * AST/ALT ≤ 2.5 × ULN (≤ 5 × ULN with documented liver metastases)
  * Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 × ULN
  * Creatinine clearance ≥ 45 mL/min
* Stable, previously treated brain metastases permitted if neurologically stable ≥ 2 weeks and on ≤ 10 mg prednisone equivalent. Untreated CNS metastases may be permitted with PI approval if: lesions are asymptomatic, ≤5 mm in size, no radiologic evidence of surrounding edema, and no current or anticipated need for corticosteroids.
* Life expectancy ≥ 12 weeks.
* Ability to swallow oral medication. TNG 462 tablets may be crushed and administered via NG-G tube if necessary, with written approval from Principal Investigator. Lorlatinib may not be crushed.
* Written informed consent obtained prior to study procedures.
* Participants must understand, sign and date the written informed consent form prior to any protocol-specific procedures performed. Participants should be able and willing to comply with study visits and procedures as per protocol

Exclusion Criteria:

* 3.2.1 Prior treatment with a PRMT5 inhibitor, MAT2A inhibitor, or any investigational agent targeting the same pathway.

3.2.2 Prior treatment with lorlatinib resulting in discontinuation due to ≥ Grade 3 toxicity or with unresolved ≥ Grade 2 neurocognitive, pulmonary, or psychiatric adverse events at screening.

3.2.3 Ongoing or unresolved toxicity \> Grade 1 from previous anticancer therapy (per CTCAE v5.0), except for the following: alopecia, endocrinopathies controlled by replacement therapy, or other protocol-allowed persistent Grade 2 toxicities (e.g., neuropathy) that, in the investigator's judgment, do not pose an unacceptable safety risk.

3.2.4 Major surgery within 4 weeks before first dose or incomplete recovery from surgery

3.2.5 Radiotherapy within 2 weeks before C1D1 (≤ 1 week for palliative RT ≤ 2 Gy/fraction); prior cranial RT permitted if completed ≥ 2 weeks before C1D1 and participant neurologically stable.

3.2.6 Concomitant use of strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors or inducers, CYP3A or P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index (e.g., digoxin, cyclosporine), or OATP1B3 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index (e.g. rosuvastatin, methotrexate, sirolimus), that cannot be discontinued or replaced.

3.2.7 Use of medications known to prolong QTc \> 480 ms that cannot be safely discontinued.

* Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis or spinal cord compression unless treated, clinically stable ≥ 4 weeks, and off steroids ≥ 14 days.
* History of seizure disorder requiring enzyme-inducing antiepileptic drugs that cannot be substituted.
* Baseline QTc \> 480 ms (Fridericia), PR \> 220 ms, clinically significant atrioventricular (AV) block, or uncontrolled arrhythmia.
* History of myocardial infarction, unstable angina, coronary revascularization, stroke, or transient ischemic attack (TIA) within 6 months before C1D1.
* Symptomatic congestive heart failure (NYHA ≥ Class II) or uncontrolled hypertension despite optimal medical therapy.
* Interstitial lung disease, organizing pneumonia, or drug-induced pneumonitis, including prior lorlatinib-related pneumonitis, unless completely resolved.
* Known HBsAg-positive or HCV RNA-positive infection with detectable viral load. Participant on suppressive antiviral therapy with undetectable viremia are eligible.
* HIV infection with CD4 \< 200/μL or on antiretrovirals that are strong CYP3A modulators.
* Active uncontrolled infection requiring intravenous therapy within 7 days before C1D1.
* Clinically significant gastrointestinal disorder that may affect absorption of oral medications (e.g., malabsorption syndrome, chronic diarrhea, short-bowel syndrome).
* Uncontrolled hyperlipidemia defined as fasting total cholesterol \> 300 mg/dL or triglycerides \> 300 mg/dL despite medical management.
* Clinically significant neurocognitive disorder, mood alteration, or psychiatric illness (including major depression or psychosis) that, in the investigator's judgment, could be exacerbated by lorlatinib or impair adherence.
* Any other active malignancy within 2 years prior to enrollment, except adequately treated basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, carcinoma in situ of the cervix, early-stage prostate cancer undergoing active surveillance, curatively treated thyroid cancer, early stage breast cancer or DCIS, or any in situ cancers that have been treated with curative intent.
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding. Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 7 days before first dose and agree to use two highly effective contraceptive methods during treatment and for ≥ 6 months after the last dose. Male participants must use effective contraception for ≥ 3 months after the last dose.
* Known hypersensitivity to TNG462, lorlatinib, or any of their excipients.
* Has any of the following: prior history of drug-induced or toxic retinopathy, or optic neuropathy; uncontrolled glaucoma; pre-existing macular degeneration; ongoing Grade ≥3 retinopathy, optic neuropathy, or optic neuritis; or any other known active retinal pathology.
* Any condition (medical, psychiatric, social, or laboratory abnormality) that, in the opinion of the investigator, may confound study results, increase risk, or interfere with study compliance.
* Participants who, in the investigator's or Sponsor-Investigator's judgment, are unable to comply with protocol requirements or whose participation would not be in their best interest may be excluded.
